title: The Monster

evidence.note: The Monster was released in 1925. The 95-year US term for 1925 publications expired at the end of 2020, so the film print has been in the US public domain since January 1, 2021. Duke CSPD states that works from 1925 entered the US public domain on that date.
evidence.source: Duke CSPD Public Domain Day 2021 (works from 1925)

evidence.note: The copyright was in fact renewed: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Motion Pictures, Jan-Dec 1953 (archive.org): 'THE MONSTER, a photoplay in seven reels by Metro-Goldwyn Pictures Corp. (c) 9Mar25, L21216. R106670, 3Feb53, Loew's Incorporated. (PWH)'. This does not change the outcome: a renewed 1925 work still tops out at the same 95-year ceiling, which expired 1 January 2021 regardless.
evidence.source: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Motion Pictures, Jan-Dec 1953 (archive.org)

evidence.note: The film is silent. The images are free, but any music on a modern copy is a separate work or recording and may be protected. Wikipedia's film page says the film has been shown on the TCM network with an alternative and uncredited musical score. Check the source of the soundtrack on any copy you use.

The film is based on Crane Wilbur's 1922 stage play of the same name (Wikipedia film page). Whether the play script was published or registered, and so what its US term is, was not confirmed. An unpublished play may be protected for the author's life plus 70 years, so the source play is not treated as cleared.
No active trademark on the title or on the Dr. Ziska character was found or checked in a trademark database. Not confirmed either way.

No dedicated modern restoration was confirmed. The Wikipedia film page mentions only a TCM presentation with an alternative, uncredited score. A faithful copy adds no new US copyright, but a new score or added titles on a restored copy would be separately protected.

renewal_search.negative_result: Not negative: the CCE 1953 motion-pictures volume shows the film WAS renewed (R106670, 3Feb53, Loew's Incorporated), see print layer evidence. Does not affect the verdict: the 95-year ceiling for a renewed 1925 work expired 1 January 2021 regardless.

editorial:
The Monster is a 1925 American silent horror-comedy directed by Roland West and starring Lon Chaney as Dr. Gustave Ziska. Johnny Arthur plays Johnny Goodlittle, an amateur detective, with Gertrude Olmstead and Hallam Cooley in support. It was distributed by Metro-Goldwyn Pictures. A creator would want it for the Chaney performance and its mix of laughs and thrills.

The film print is in the US public domain because the 95-year term for 1925 publications expired at the end of 2020, even though the copyright was renewed in 1953 by Loew's Incorporated. The trap is the layers around the print. Any score on a modern copy is a separate work. The film adapts Crane Wilbur's 1922 stage play, and whether that play was published, and so when its term ends, was not confirmed. Check the play before you adapt the story rather than just reusing the film.
faq: Can I use footage from The Monster (1925) in my own video?

Yes for the picture itself. The 1925 film print is public domain in the US because its term has expired. Use a copy without added music, or a score you have cleared. A recorded score on a modern copy belongs to whoever made it.
Can I remake or adapt The Monster?

Remaking the story is a different question from using the print. The film is based on Crane Wilbur's 1922 play, and whether that script was published or what its term is was not confirmed. Check the play's copyright status first. Do not assume the film's status covers it.
